messages:
Alex: Heads-up — need consolidated inputs from hardware partners for the upcoming cost model refresh. Key gaps: regional spot eviction rates, minimum commit windows, premium for SLA-backed reserved pools. Anyone already collected vendor-level numbers?
Maria: I pulled emails from CoreWeave & VoltCloud last week. CoreWeave gave a multi-tier reserve ladder but omitted regional eviction curves. VoltCloud returned a CSV for pricing tiers but no listing fee info. I can share. :email:
Jon: Important we standardize the SKU mapping. Different partners call the same GPU class different names (A100-40GB vs a100x). If we don't normalize, our model will double-count capacity.
Rachel: Marketplace fees: Azure/Google marketplace show a 6-12% listing/transaction fee depending on billing flow. That matters for the hosted offering. Also need to confirm whether partner credits reduce reported revenue or are line-item discounts.
Kevin: I sketched a compact CSV schema for ingestion. Paste: ```vendor,region,sku,commit_tier_min_hours,commit_tier_max_hours,reserved_price_usd_per_hour,spot_price_usd_per_hour,eviction_rate_pct,lead_time_days,listing_fee_pct,notes``` Use this when you send vendor data back.
Alex: Nice, Kevin. Maria — can you ask CoreWeave for eviction by region (us-west/us-east/eu-central + aapac) and whether they have a preemption SLA for reserved pools?
Maria: On it. Also flagged that some partners only report median eviction windows, not full percentiles. Will ask for 95th pct.
Jon: For modeling, we need: 1) historical spot price variance (30/90/365d), 2) eviction probability by time in use, 3) min scaleable chunk (how small a reservation can be). That lets us compute expected utilization and blended unit cost.
Rachel: Also check commit cancellation penalties and how quickly capacity can be repurposed. Marketplaces often prevent immediate re-listing which affects our ability to reclaim idle reserved nodes.
Alex: Action items: Maria — vendor follow-ups (CoreWeave, VoltCloud, Zenith) by Tue EOD. Jon — build SKU normalization table template and share in repo. Kevin — add the CSV schema to the cost-model repo and a small parser that validates ranges. Rachel — confirm marketplace fee treatment with finance.
Maria: Quick note on Zenith: their sales contact mentioned a short-term promotional premium (10% off reserved price) if we can commit 6+ months, but they require 30d notice for termination. Will confirm exact terms.
Jon: If vendors provide only aggregate numbers, we'll need to run scenario runs (conservative / base / optimistic) with assumed variance. Let's keep assumptions explicit per vendor so procurement can negotiate.
Kevin: I'll add a column `assumption_bucket` to the schema (conservative|base|optimistic) and `source_doc_link` for traceability.
Rachel: Can someone flag which partners have SOC2/PIF requirements that might change pricing (e.g., private deployment surcharge)? I remember VoltCloud applies a +15% for air-gapped.
Alex: Good call. Add that as `regulatory_surcharge_pct` in the schema. Last thing — timeline: need draft numbers in the model by next Friday for the exec QBR. Prioritize partners with largest committed capacity.
Maria: Will prioritize CoreWeave and VoltCloud. I'll post vendor replies in this thread as they come. :thumbsup:
Jon: I'll start the normalization work today and link the PR.
Kevin: Schema + validator PR incoming in ~2 hours.
Rachel: I'll sync with finance on marketplace fee treatment and confirm whether credits are grossed or netted.
Alex: Thanks team — let's keep updates short here so we have a single source. If partners push contracts, drop them into the secure drive and ping me.
Maria: Uploaded VoltCloud CSV and CoreWeave email convo to the drive, link: https://drive.redwood.internal/partners/q2-cost-inputs (shared with procurement).
Jon: Saw the CSV. VoltCloud's spot price column uses hourly floats but they left `eviction_rate_pct` empty — Maria, can you chase that specifically?
Maria: Yup, flagged it in my follow-up.
Alex: Great. That should be everything for now. We'll reconvene next Thurs if needed.
